questions.title: What CSS is
questions.text: Describe the purpose of **CSS** in web design.

scheme.mark_scheme:
- CSS describes how HTML elements are displayed / the presentation: colours, fonts, spacing, layout (1)
- it separates style from content / one style sheet can control many pages, giving a consistent design that is easy to change (1)

points.criterion: Controls the appearance of HTML elements
Separation of style / consistency / easy changes

scheme.model_answer: CSS describes how the HTML elements look — their colours, fonts, spacing and layout — and keeps the style separate from the content, so one style sheet can give a whole website a consistent design.

scheme.model_answer: 1 Inline CSS is written in the style attribute of one element, whereas external CSS is in a separate file linked to many pages. 2 With external CSS the whole site is changed by editing one file, whereas inline styles must be changed in every element.

scheme.mark_scheme:
- A class (.name) can be applied to many elements on a page / reused (1)
- An ID (#name) must be unique — used for one element only; IDs have higher specificity (1)

points.criterion: ID: one unique element, written with #

scheme.model_answer: A class selector, written with a dot, can style many elements that share the class, whereas an ID selector, written with #, styles one unique element.

- margin is the space outside the border, between the element and other elements (1)

questions.title: Inheritance
questions.text: A developer writes `body { font-family: Arial; color: #333; }`. Explain why the paragraphs and headings on the page also use Arial.

scheme.mark_scheme:
- Text properties such as font-family / color are inherited (1)
- by child elements of body (paragraphs, headings) unless a more specific rule changes them (1)

points.criterion: Children of body inherit unless overridden

scheme.model_answer: Font and colour properties are inherited, so every element inside the body, such as paragraphs and headings, takes the body's font unless another rule sets a different one.

questions.title: Responsive design

scheme.mark_scheme:
- On screens 600 px wide or less, the boxes in .container are placed one under another (column) (1)

scheme.model_answer: When the screen is 600 px wide or less, the items in the container are shown one under another instead of side by side, so the page fits and is easy to read on a phone.

theory.title: What CSS is and why it is used

blocks.content: A style-sheet language that describes **how HTML elements are displayed** — colours, fonts, sizes, spacing, borders, backgrounds and layout. HTML gives the **structure and content**; CSS gives the **presentation**.

items.title: Why separate style from content?
items.content:
- The **same HTML** can be shown with different designs (e.g. for screens and for printing).
- One style sheet can control the look of **a whole website** — consistent design.
- Changes are **quick**: edit one rule instead of every page.
- HTML files are **smaller and cleaner**, so they are easier to read and maintain.
- Pages load faster because an external style sheet is **cached** by the browser.

items.title: What CSS can control
items.content:
- Text: font, size, colour, weight, alignment, decoration.
- Boxes: width, height, margin, padding, border, rounded corners.
- Backgrounds: colours, images, gradients.
- Layout: positioning, columns, flexbox, grid.
- Effects: hover states, transitions, responsive design for phones.

theory.title: The three ways to add CSS

items.title: Inline CSS
items.content:
Written in the **`style` attribute** of **one element**. `

Warning

`

items.title: Internal (embedded) CSS
items.content:
Written in a **`<style>` element** in the **`<head>`** of **one page**.
`<style> p { color: red; } </style>`

items.title: External CSS
items.content:
Written in a **separate `.css` file** that is **linked** to many pages with `<link>` in the `<head>`.
`<link rel="stylesheet" href="style.css">`

items.title: Advantages of external CSS
items.content:
- One file controls the **whole site** → consistent design.
- Change the design of hundreds of pages by editing **one file**.
- Smaller HTML pages; the CSS file is **cached**, so later pages load faster.
- Different style sheets can be linked for different devices / printing.

items.title: Disadvantages of external CSS
items.content:
- An **extra file** must be downloaded before the page is styled.
- If the file is missing or the link is wrong, the page appears **unstyled**.
- For a single small page it may be unnecessary.

blocks.content: Give **both sides** each time: "*External CSS is stored in a separate file that **all pages** link to, so the whole site can be changed by editing **one file**, **whereas** inline CSS must be written in **every element**, which is slow to change and makes pages inconsistent.*"

Book Club

blocks.content:
- A **colon** separates the property and the value: `color: red` (not `color = red`).
- A **semicolon** ends each declaration: `color: red; font-size: 14px;`.
- Rules are written in **curly braces** `{ }`.
- A class selector starts with `.`, an ID selector with `#`.
- The browser simply **ignores** a rule it cannot understand — no error message is shown.
When several rules set the same property of the same element, the browser must decide which one **wins** — this is the **cascade**.

blocks.title: How the browser chooses the winning rule
items: **Specificity** — the more **specific** selector wins: **inline style > ID > class / pseudo-class > element**.
**Order** — if specificity is equal, the rule that comes **later** wins (so a `<style>` block placed after the `<link>` overrides the external file).

blocks.title: Which colour is the paragraph?
blocks.content:
```html

Welcome

``` Rules: `p { color: gray; }`, `.lead { color: orange; }`, `#intro { color: blue; }` → the text is **blue**, because the **ID selector is the most specific**. If the paragraph also had `style="color: green"`, it would be **green** (inline wins).

Some properties — mostly **text** properties such as `color`, `font-family` and `font-size` — are **inherited** by child elements. Setting `body { font-family: Arial; }` makes every element on the page use Arial unless a more specific rule changes it. Box properties such as `border`, `margin` and `width` are **not** inherited.

items.title: Flexbox for layout
items.content: `display: flex;` places child boxes **in a row** (or a column with `flex-direction: column;`). `gap` sets the space between them, `justify-content` and `align-items` align them. It is the easiest way to build menus and card layouts.

items.title: Responsive design
items.content: A **media query** `@media (max-width: 600px) { … }` applies rules only on small screens, so the same page works on phones and computers. Use relative widths (`%`) and the viewport meta tag `<meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1">`.

blocks.title: Good design practice with CSS
rows: Use **one external style sheet** for all pages
Use **classes** for repeated styles, IDs only for unique elements
Limit the number of fonts and colours
Ensure good **contrast** between text and background
Users can see what is clickable
Test on **different screen sizes and browsers**
The design works for every user

blocks.title: Exam-style answers
blocks.content:
**Q: Create a CSS rule for changing the colour of the heading text to red and underlining it. [3]**
```css
h1 {
    color: red;
    text-decoration: underline;
}
```
`h1` (1), `color: red;` (1), `text-decoration: underline;` (1).

**Q: Compare inline and external CSS. [2]**
Inline CSS is written in the **style attribute of a single element**, **whereas** external CSS is in a **separate file linked to every page** (1). External CSS lets the whole site be updated by **changing one file**, whereas inline styles must be changed **in every element** (1).

**Q: Write the HTML code to link the style sheet `site.css` to a page. [1]**
`<link rel="stylesheet" href="site.css">` inside the `<head>`.

**Q: Write a CSS rule so that links in the navigation bar are not underlined and turn white on a blue background when the mouse is over them. [3]**
`nav a { text-decoration: none; }` (1) `nav a:hover { color: white; background-color: blue; }` (selector 1, declarations 1).

- Using `=` instead of `:` or forgetting `;` between declarations.
- Writing `.` before an ID or `#` before a class.
- Using the **same ID** on several elements — use a **class**.
- Putting the `<link>` or `<style>` in the `<body>` instead of the `<head>`.
- Saying external CSS has the highest priority — **inline** styles override it.
- Writing `colour` (British spelling) — CSS uses **`color`**.
